# Renewal Runway — User Stories

## Calculation Rules

These rules govern every result the app produces. All stories are written against them.

**Credit precision**  
Credits are stored as integer hundredths (1.5 credits = 150 units). All arithmetic uses integers, eliminating floating-point errors.

**Credits remaining**  
`remaining = max(required − earned, 0)`. When earned ≥ required the result is 0 for pace purposes; the panel shows the requirement-met state instead.

**Days left**  
`days_left = end_date − calculate_from_date + 1` (both dates inclusive).  
Example: Dec 29 → Dec 31 = 3 days. This reflects that credits can be earned on the last day of the cycle.

**Weekly pace**  
`pace = remaining ÷ days_left × 7`, rounded **up** to 2 decimal places. Rounding up ensures that sustaining the shown pace always finishes on time.

**Date display**  
Calendar dates only; no time-of-day or time-zone handling. Shown as "Dec 31, 2027".

**Number display**  
Up to 2 decimal places; trailing zeros dropped (4.00 → 4, 3.90 → 3.9); thousands separators applied. Exactly 1 uses the singular form ("1 credit", "1 day"); all other quantities use the plural.

**Live updates**  
Results update as fields change. There is no separate calculate button.

**Certification presets**  
Selecting a preset fills credits required. Manually editing credits required switches the selector to Custom.

| Preset | Credits required |
|---|---|
| SHRM-CP / SHRM-SCP | 60 |
| HRCI PHR / SPHR | 60 |
| PMI PMP | 60 |
| PMI CAPM | 15 |
| Custom | (user-entered) |

Presets cover totals only; category or activity-type breakdowns are out of scope.

**Field limits**

| Field | Valid range |
|---|---|
| Credits required | > 0 and ≤ 500, up to 2 decimal places |
| Credits earned | ≥ 0 and ≤ 1,000, up to 2 decimal places |
| Cycle end date | Valid calendar date, year 2000–2100 |
| Calculate-from date | Valid calendar date, year 2000–2100 |

**Default state (on load and after reset)**  
Preset: Custom. Credits required: empty. Credits earned: 0. Cycle end date: empty. Calculate-from date: current date. No result is shown until credits required and cycle end date are both filled with valid values.

---

## Results panel — priority order

When credits required and cycle end date are both valid, the panel shows exactly one of these states, checked in this order:

1. **Requirement met** — earned ≥ required. Shown even if the deadline has passed.
2. **Deadline passed** — cycle end date is before the calculate-from date and requirement not met.
3. **Urgency** — days left < 7 and requirement not met.
4. **Weekly pace** — all other cases.

An at-risk warning appears above the result for states 3 and 4 when the weekly pace exceeds 40. A pace of exactly 40 is not at risk.

---

Each story below names the job it serves. Status reflects what the app does today.

---

## S-1 · Enter certification details and see weekly pace
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want to enter my total credits required, credits already earned, and certification cycle end date and see the weekly pace I need from today, so that I can plan how many hours of training to schedule each week.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027 (70 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 20, then pace shows as **"4 credits per week"** (remaining 40 ÷ 70 × 7 = 4.0, trailing zero dropped).
- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 14, 2027 (73 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 20, then pace shows as **"3.84 credits per week"** (40 ÷ 73 × 7 = 3.836…, rounded up to 3.84).
- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027 (70 days); required = 60; earned = 59.99, then pace shows as **"0.01 credits per week"** (remaining 0.01 ÷ 70 × 7 = 0.001, rounded up to 0.01).
- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Dec 30, 2027 (364 days); required = 500; earned = 0, then pace shows as **"9.62 credits per week"** (500 ÷ 364 × 7 = 9.615…, rounded up), confirming the app handles maximum field values without error.
- Given credits required = 501, then a field-level error appears and no result is shown.
- Given credits required = 500; calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027 (70 days); earned = 0, then pace shows as **"50 credits per week"** (no error at the upper boundary; 500 ÷ 70 × 7 = 50.0).
- Given credits required = 0, then a field-level error appears and no result is shown.
- Given credits earned = −1, then a field-level error appears and no result is shown.
- Given credits earned = 1,001, then a field-level error appears and no result is shown.
- Given credits required = "abc" (non-numeric), then a field-level error appears and no result is shown.
- Given cycle end date = Feb 30, 2027 (not a valid calendar date), then a field-level error appears and no result is shown.
- Given cycle end date year = 1999, then a field-level error appears and no result is shown.
- Given credits earned is left empty; calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027; required = 60, then earned is treated as 0 and pace shows as **"6 credits per week"** (60 ÷ 70 × 7 = 6.0).
- Given credits required = 501 (error showing), when credits required is corrected to 60 and end = Mar 11, 2027 and calc-from = Jan 1, 2027 and earned = 20, then the error clears and **"4 credits per week"** appears.
- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027; required = 60; earned = 20 (result "4 credits per week" is showing), when cycle end date is cleared, then the result disappears immediately.

---

## S-2 · See an urgency message when fewer than 7 days remain
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-2 | **Status:** Implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want to see the credits I still need stated in days rather than weeks when my deadline is very close, so that I can judge immediately whether catching up is still feasible.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given calc-from = Dec 26, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027 (6 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 50, then the panel shows **"you need 10 credits in the next 6 days"** with no at-risk warning (equivalent pace 10 ÷ 6 × 7 = 11.67, which is ≤ 40).
- Given calc-from = Dec 30, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027 (2 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 50, then the panel shows **"you need 10 credits in the next 2 days"**.
- Given calc-from = Dec 31, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027 (1 day inclusive); required = 60; earned = 50, then the at-risk warning appears and the panel shows **"you need 10 credits today"** (equivalent pace 10 ÷ 1 × 7 = 70, which is > 40).
- Given calc-from = Dec 25, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027 (7 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 50, then the panel shows the weekly pace **"10 credits per week"** (10 ÷ 7 × 7 = 10.0) — urgency is not triggered at exactly 7 days.

---

## S-3 · Confirm that the credit requirement is met
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-3 | **Status:** Implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want to see a clear confirmation when my earned credits meet or exceed the total required, so that I can submit my renewal without second-guessing the numbers.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 60, then the requirement-met confirmation is shown.
- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 65 (5 credits beyond the requirement), then the requirement-met confirmation is shown.
- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2028; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 60 (deadline already passed), then the requirement-met confirmation is shown — not the deadline-passed message.
- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027 (70 days); required = 60; earned = 59.99, then the requirement-met confirmation is **not** shown and pace shows as "0.01 credits per week" instead (59.99 < 60).

---

## S-4 · Know when the cycle has ended without the requirement being met
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-2 | **Status:** Implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want to know clearly when my certification cycle has ended without my having met the credit requirement, so that I understand my situation and can decide what to do next.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2028; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 50, then the panel shows **"Cycle ended on Dec 31, 2027 (1 day ago)"** with no pace shown (Jan 1 2028 − Dec 31 2027 = 1 day).
- Given calc-from = Jan 31, 2028; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 50, then the panel shows **"Cycle ended on Dec 31, 2027 (31 days ago)"**.
- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2028; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 60, then the requirement-met confirmation is shown — not the deadline-passed message.

---

## S-5 · See an at-risk warning when the required pace is unsustainable
**Role:** L&D Manager | **Job:** J-4 | **Status:** Implemented

As an L&D Manager, I want to see a prominent at-risk warning when the credits-per-week pace exceeds 40, so that I can immediately identify a team member who needs intervention before it is too late.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027 (70 days); required = 500; earned = 100, then pace shows as **"40 credits per week"** (remaining 400 ÷ 70 × 7 = 40.0) with **no at-risk warning** — exactly 40 is not at risk.
- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027 (70 days); required = 500; earned = 99, then the **at-risk warning appears** above **"40.1 credits per week"** (remaining 401 ÷ 70 × 7 = 40.1).
- Given calc-from = Dec 31, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027 (1 day); required = 60; earned = 50, then the **at-risk warning appears** above **"you need 10 credits today"** (equivalent pace 10 ÷ 1 × 7 = 70).
- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 60, then no at-risk warning appears (requirement already met).
- Given calc-from = Jan 31, 2028; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 50, then no at-risk warning appears (deadline-passed state).

---

## S-6 · Set a future calculate-from date to model a later start
**Role:** L&D Manager | **Job:** J-5 | **Status:** Implemented

As an L&D Manager, I want to set the calculate-from date to a future date, so that I can model the pace a team member would need if their dedicated training time started next quarter and decide where to commit budget before the quarter begins.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given calc-from = Dec 1, 2027; end = Jan 9, 2028 (40 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 20, then pace shows as **"7 credits per week"** (40 ÷ 40 × 7 = 7.0) — this is the reference result showing calculate-from affects days_left.
- Given calc-from = Apr 1, 2027; end = Jun 29, 2027 (90 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 24, then pace shows as **"2.8 credits per week"** (remaining 36 ÷ 90 × 7 = 2.8). With calc-from = Jan 1, 2027 instead (180 days inclusive), the same end date and credits yield **"1.4 credits per week"** (36 ÷ 180 × 7 = 1.4), showing how a later start doubles the required pace.
- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2028; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 50, then the deadline-passed state is shown — a calculate-from date after the cycle end is valid input, not an error.
- Given calc-from = Feb 28, 2028; end = Mar 1, 2028 (3 days inclusive — 2028 is a leap year, so Feb 29 is counted); required = 60; earned = 57, then pace shows as **"7 credits per week"** (remaining 3 ÷ 3 × 7 = 7.0). With calc-from = Feb 28, 2027 and end = Mar 1, 2027 instead (2 days inclusive — 2027 is not a leap year), the same credits yield **"10.5 credits per week"** (3 ÷ 2 × 7 = 10.5), confirming Feb 29 is counted when it exists.

---

## S-7 · Compare renewal status across multiple team members
**Role:** L&D Manager | **Job:** J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented

As an L&D Manager, I want to enter details for several team members in one view and see them ranked by risk, so that I can prioritise training budget across the team without running separate calculations.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given two team members are entered, one at-risk and one on track, when I view the team list, then the at-risk member appears first.
- Given a team member's data changes, then their position in the ranked list updates immediately.

---

## S-8 · Select a certification preset to fill credits required
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want to pick my credential from a list and have the total credits required filled in automatically, so that I do not have to look up the number for my specific certification.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given I select SHRM-CP / SHRM-SCP, then credits required is set to 60.
- Given I select PMI CAPM, then credits required is set to 15.
- Given I select a preset and then manually edit credits required, then the selector switches to Custom.
- Given I select a preset, manually edit credits required, and then select the same preset again, then credits required returns to the preset value.

---

## S-9 · Reset all fields to the default state
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want to clear all inputs and return to the starting state, so that I can run a fresh calculation without reloading the page.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given any fields have been changed, when I activate reset, then credits required is cleared, credits earned returns to 0, cycle end date is cleared, calculate-from date returns to the current date, and the preset selector returns to Custom.
- Given a result or error is currently shown, when I activate reset, then it is cleared immediately and no result is shown.

---

## S-10 · Track credits by required category
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-3 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want to enter my credits broken down by required category so that I can confirm I have met each category minimum, not just the overall total.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given a PMP credential with Talent Triangle minimums (Technical, Leadership, Strategic & Business), when I enter credits by category, then I see whether each minimum is satisfied alongside the overall total.
- Given an HRCI credential with an ethics credit requirement, when I enter my credits, then the ethics component is verified separately from the total.

---

## S-11 · Save inputs between visits
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want my certification details to be remembered when I return to the app, so that I do not have to re-enter them every time I check my pace.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given I have entered credits required, credits earned, and a cycle end date, when I close and reopen the app, then those values are restored and the result is shown immediately.
- Given I activate reset, when I close and reopen the app, then no saved values are restored and the app shows the default state.

---

## S-12 · See how many courses to complete each week
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want to see my weekly pace expressed as a number of courses, not just credits, so that I can turn the target into a concrete item on my calendar.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given a weekly pace of 2 credits and a typical course length of 1 credit, then the result shows "2 courses per week" alongside the credit pace.
- Given I can set a typical course length, when I change it, then the courses-per-week figure updates immediately.

# Renewal Runway — Jobs To Be Done

## J-1 · Plan a manageable training pace (R-1 Certified Professional)

When I am part-way through my recertification cycle and unsure how much training I still need to do, I want to know how many credits I need to earn per week from now until my deadline, so I can fit learning around work at a steady rate instead of rushing at the end.

## J-2 · Quickly assess whether a late renewal is still realistic (R-1 Certified Professional)

When my deadline is close and I know I am behind on credits, I want to know immediately whether hitting the required total in the time remaining is feasible, so I can decide whether to clear my calendar, pursue an exam route, or plan around the grace period.

## J-3 · Confirm the requirement is met and close the loop (R-1 Certified Professional)

When I have earned most of my credits and believe I may have reached the required total, I want to confirm my earned credits meet or exceed the requirement, so I can stop tracking and submit my renewal with confidence.

## J-4 · Spot at-risk team members before it is too late (R-2 L&D Manager)

When I am reviewing my team's professional development status, I want to know which team members are unlikely to reach their recertification requirement by their deadline, so I can act while there is still enough time for training to make a difference.

## J-5 · Plan training allocation for a future quarter (R-2 L&D Manager)

When I am deciding how to allocate training time and budget for an upcoming quarter, I want to know what pace a team member would need to meet their recertification requirement if their dedicated learning time started then rather than now, so I can compare options and commit resources to where they will have the most impact.

# Renewal Runway — App Roles

## R-1 · Certified Professional

A Certified Professional is a credentialed HR or project-management practitioner who is responsible for renewing their own certification before their cycle ends. They know their total credit requirement and their cycle end date, and they check in on their own progress when they feel uncertain about whether they are keeping up. They can enter their certification details — credits required, credits already earned, and cycle end date — and see their required weekly pace from today and a risk assessment for their renewal. They must never be told they are on track, or that their renewal is complete, when their actual credit figures say otherwise.

## R-2 · L&D Manager

An L&D Manager is a learning-and-development or team manager who monitors recertification progress for people who report to them. They are checking someone else's renewal: they read credit figures from that person's certification portal and work in quarterly planning windows rather than reacting to today's status. They can enter a team member's certification details and choose a future "calculate from" date to model what pace the team member would need if training time started next quarter or later. Their primary output is the risk flag — they use it to decide where to direct training budget and protected learning time. They must never receive a result that shows a renewal as low-risk or on track when the underlying figures indicate the team member is at risk of missing their deadline.

Please analyze this codebase and create a CLAUDE.md file, which will be given to future instances of Claude Code to operate in this repository.

What to add:
1. Commands that will be commonly used, such as how to build, lint, and run tests. Include the necessary commands to develop in this codebase, such as how to run a single test.
2. High-level code architecture and structure so that future instances can be productive more quickly. Focus on the "big picture" architecture that requires reading multiple files to understand.

Usage notes:
- If there's already a CLAUDE.md, suggest improvements to it.
- When you make the initial CLAUDE.md, do not repeat yourself and do not include obvious instructions like "Provide helpful error messages to users", "Write unit tests for all new utilities", "Never include sensitive information (API keys, tokens) in code or commits".
- Avoid listing every component or file structure that can be easily discovered.
- Don't include generic development practices.
- If there are Cursor rules (in .cursor/rules/ or .cursorrules) or Copilot rules (in .github/copilot-instructions.md), make sure to include the important parts.
- If there is a README.md, make sure to include the important parts.
- Do not make up information such as "Common Development Tasks", "Tips for Development", "Support and Documentation" unless this is expressly included in other files that you read.
- Be sure to prefix the file with the following text:

```
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
```

# Renewal Runway — User Stories

## Calculation Rules

These rules govern every result the app produces. All stories are written against them.

**Credit precision**  
Credits are stored as integer hundredths (1.5 credits = 150 units). All arithmetic uses integers, eliminating floating-point errors.

**Credits remaining**  
`remaining = max(required − earned, 0)`. When earned ≥ required the result is 0 for pace purposes; the panel shows the requirement-met state instead.

**Days left**  
`days_left = end_date − calculate_from_date + 1` (both dates inclusive).  
Example: Dec 29 → Dec 31 = 3 days. This reflects that credits can be earned on the last day of the cycle.

**Weekly pace**  
`pace = remaining ÷ days_left × 7`, rounded **up** to 2 decimal places. Rounding up ensures that sustaining the shown pace always finishes on time.

**Date display**  
Calendar dates only; no time-of-day or time-zone handling. Shown as "Dec 31, 2027".

**Number display**

**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-2 | **Status:** Implemented

**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-3 | **Status:** Implemented

**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-2 | **Status:** Implemented

- Given calc-from = Jan 31, 2028; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 50, then the panel shows **"Cycle ended on Dec 31, 2027 (31 days ago)."**

**Role:** L&D Manager | **Job:** J-4 | **Status:** Implemented

## S-7 · Input validation
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want the app to flag invalid entries immediately with a clear message, so that I am never shown a result based on nonsense inputs and I know exactly what to fix.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given credits required = 501, then the error **"Credits required cannot exceed 500."** appears and no result is shown.
- Given credits required = "abc" (non-numeric), then the error **"Credits required must be a number."** appears and no result is shown.
- Given credits required = 60.555, then the error **"Credits required cannot have more than 2 decimal places."** appears and no result is shown.
- Given credits earned = −1, then the error **"Credits earned cannot be negative."** appears and no result is shown.
- Given credits earned = 1,001, then the error **"Credits earned cannot exceed 1,000."** appears and no result is shown.
- Given credits earned = "abc" (non-numeric), then the error **"Credits earned must be a number."** appears and no result is shown.
- Given credits earned = 60.555, then the error **"Credits earned cannot have more than 2 decimal places."** appears and no result is shown.
- Given cycle end date year = 1999, then the error **"Cycle end date must be between 2000 and 2100."** appears and no result is shown.
- Given cycle end date year = 2101, then the error **"Cycle end date must be between 2000 and 2100."** appears and no result is shown.
- Given the calculate-from date is cleared, then the error **"Calculate-from date is required."** appears and no result is shown.
- Given cycle end date is empty and credits required = 60 and calc-from = Jan 1, 2027, then no error appears for the end date field and no result is shown.
- Given credits required = 501 (error showing), when credits required is corrected to 60 and end = Mar 11, 2027 and calc-from = Jan 1, 2027 and earned = 20, then the error clears and **"4 credits per week"** appears.
- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027; required = 60; earned = 20 (result "4 credits per week" is showing), when cycle end date is cleared, then the result disappears immediately and no error is shown for the end date field.

---

## S-8 · Select a certification preset to fill credits required
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want to pick my credential from a list and have the total credits required filled in automatically, so that I do not have to look up the number for my specific certification.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given I select SHRM-CP / SHRM-SCP, then credits required is set to 60.
- Given I select PMI CAPM, then credits required is set to 15.
- Given I select a preset and then manually edit credits required, then the selector switches to Custom.
- Given I select a preset, manually edit credits required, and then select the same preset again, then credits required returns to the preset value.

---

## S-9 · Reset all fields to the default state
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want to clear all inputs and return to the starting state, so that I can run a fresh calculation without reloading the page.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given any fields have been changed, when I activate reset, then credits required is cleared, credits earned returns to 0, cycle end date is cleared, calculate-from date returns to the current date (read at reset time, not page-load time), and the preset selector returns to Custom.
- Given a result or error is currently shown, when I activate reset, then it is cleared immediately and no result is shown.

---

## S-10 · Compare renewal status across multiple team members
**Role:** L&D Manager | **Job:** J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented

As an L&D Manager, I want to enter details for several team members in one view and see them ranked by risk, so that I can prioritise training budget across the team without running separate calculations.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given two team members are entered, one at-risk and one on track, when I view the team list, then the at-risk member appears first.
- Given a team member's data changes, then their position in the ranked list updates immediately.

---

## S-11 · Track credits by required category
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-3 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want to enter my credits broken down by required category so that I can confirm I have met each category minimum, not just the overall total.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given a PMP credential with Talent Triangle minimums (Technical, Leadership, Strategic & Business), when I enter credits by category, then I see whether each minimum is satisfied alongside the overall total.
- Given an HRCI credential with an ethics credit requirement, when I enter my credits, then the ethics component is verified separately from the total.

---

## S-12 · Save inputs between visits
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want my certification details to be remembered when I return to the app, so that I do not have to re-enter them every time I check my pace.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given I have entered credits required, credits earned, and a cycle end date, when I close and reopen the app, then those values are restored and the result is shown immediately.
- Given I activate reset, when I close and reopen the app, then no saved values are restored and the app shows the default state.

---

## S-13 · See how many courses to complete each week
**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Certified Professional, I want to see my weekly pace expressed as a number of courses, not just credits, so that I can turn the target into a concrete item on my calendar.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Given a weekly pace of 2 credits and a typical course length of 1 credit, then the result shows "2 courses per week" alongside the credit pace.
- Given I can set a typical course length, when I change it, then the courses-per-week figure updates immediately.

These rules govern every result the app produces. All stories are written against them.

Credits are stored as integer hundredths (1.5 credits = 150 units). All arithmetic uses integers, eliminating floating-point errors.

`remaining = max(required − earned, 0)`. When earned ≥ required the result is 0 for pace purposes; the panel shows the requirement-met state instead.

**Days left**  
`days_left = end_date − calculate_from_date + 1` (both dates inclusive).  
Example: Dec 29 → Dec 31 = 3 days. This reflects that credits can be earned on the last day of the cycle.

`pace = remaining ÷ days_left × 7`, rounded **up** to 2 decimal places. Rounding up ensures that sustaining the shown pace always finishes on time.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project

Renewal Runway — a browser-based recertification pace calculator for HR and project-management professionals tracking credits toward credential renewal (SHRM, HRCI, PMI). The product spec lives in `docs/`.

## Tech approach

Plain HTML + CSS + JavaScript, no framework, no build step. The app must open by double-clicking `src/index.html` in a browser — no server, no install. Keep everything in a single HTML file unless a natural split emerges (e.g. a separate `style.css` or `calc.js`). Do not introduce a bundler, package manager, or transpiler without asking first.

## Running and testing

No build step. Open `src/index.html` directly in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari.

There is no test runner yet. If tests are added, document the command here.

## Calculation rules (critical)

These rules are the source of truth for all arithmetic. They are also in `docs/user-stories.md` under "Calculation Rules".

- **Credit precision:** store credits as integer hundredths (1.5 credits → 150). Do all arithmetic in integers to avoid float errors. Only convert back to display units for output.
- **Credits remaining:** `max(required − earned, 0)`. Never negative.
- **Days left:** `end_date − calculate_from_date + 1` (both dates inclusive). Dec 29 → Dec 31 = 3 days.
- **Weekly pace:** `remaining / days_left × 7`, rounded **up** to 2 decimal places (`Math.ceil(x * 100) / 100`). Rounding up ensures the shown pace always finishes on time.
- **At-risk threshold:** pace **strictly greater than** 40. Exactly 40 is not at-risk.
- **Number display:** trailing zeros dropped (4.00 → "4", 3.90 → "3.9"), thousands separators, singular for exactly 1 ("1 credit", "1 day").
- **Date display:** "Dec 31, 2027" format.

## Results panel — priority order

Check these states in order and show the first that matches:

1. **Requirement met** — earned ≥ required (even if deadline has passed).
2. **Deadline passed** — cycle end date < calculate-from date and requirement not met.
3. **Urgency** — days left < 7 and requirement not met. Show credits needed in days, not weeks. Special-case days left = 1 as "today".
4. **Weekly pace** — all other cases.

At-risk warning appears above state 3 or 4 (never on 1 or 2) when pace > 40.

No result is shown until both credits required and cycle end date contain valid values.

## Inputs and defaults

| Field | Default | Limits |
|---|---|---|
| Preset selector | Custom | SHRM-CP/SCP 60, HRCI PHR/SPHR 60, PMI PMP 60, PMI CAPM 15, Custom |
| Credits required | empty | > 0 and ≤ 500, up to 2 decimal places |
| Credits earned | 0 | ≥ 0 and ≤ 1,000, up to 2 decimal places |
| Cycle end date | empty | valid date, year 2000–2100 |
| Calculate-from date | today | valid date, year 2000–2100 |

Selecting a preset overwrites credits required. Manually editing credits required switches preset to Custom. Reset restores all defaults; calculate-from date goes back to today (re-read at reset time, not page-load time).

Updates are live — there is no calculate button.

## Submission format

The assignment requires this layout:

```
muhammad-ahsan-calculator/
  README.md
  CLAUDE.md
  src/
  docs/
    app-roles.md
    jobs-to-be-done.md
    user-stories.md
  transcripts/
    session-01.md
```

"""Verify every numeric acceptance criterion in docs/user-stories.md."""
import sys
from datetime import date

# ── core calculation functions ───────────────────────────────────────────────

def days_left(end, frm):
    """Inclusive day count: end_date - calc_from_date + 1."""
    return (end - frm).days + 1

def days_ago(end, frm):
    """calc_from_date - end_date (deadline already passed)."""
    return (frm - end).days

def to_units(credits):
    """Credits -> integer hundredths."""
    return round(credits * 100)

def to_credits(units):
    return units / 100

def remaining_units(req_units, earned_units):
    return max(req_units - earned_units, 0)

def calc_pace(rem_units, dl):
    """Ceiling division in integer hundredths -> display credits (float)."""
    numerator = rem_units * 7
    pace_units = (numerator + dl - 1) // dl
    return to_credits(pace_units)

def is_urgency(dl):
    return dl < 7

def is_at_risk(pace):
    return pace > 40

def fmt(n):
    """Format: trailing zeros dropped, singular for 1."""
    s = f"{n:.2f}".rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
    return s

# ── test harness ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

checks = []
failures = 0

def check(label, got, expected):
    global failures
    ok = (got == expected)
    status = "PASS" if ok else "FAIL"
    print(f"{status}: {label}")
    if not ok:
        failures += 1
        print(f"       expected {expected!r}, got {got!r}")
    checks.append(ok)

def check_approx(label, got, expected):
    """Float equality with tiny epsilon."""
    ok = abs(got - expected) < 1e-9
    global failures
    status = "PASS" if ok else "FAIL"
    print(f"{status}: {label}")
    if not ok:
        failures += 1
        print(f"       expected {expected!r}, got {got!r}")
    checks.append(ok)

# ── S-1 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("=== S-1: Weekly pace ===")

# AC1: 70 days, 40 remaining -> 4.0
dl = days_left(date(2027,3,11), date(2027,1,1))
check("S-1 AC1 days_left=70", dl, 70)
pace = calc_pace(to_units(40), dl)
check("S-1 AC1 pace=4", pace, 4.0)
check("S-1 AC1 not at-risk", is_at_risk(pace), False)
check("S-1 AC1 not urgency", is_urgency(dl), False)

# AC2: 73 days, 40 remaining -> 3.84
dl = days_left(date(2027,3,14), date(2027,1,1))
check("S-1 AC2 days_left=73", dl, 73)
pace = calc_pace(to_units(40), dl)
check("S-1 AC2 pace=3.84", pace, 3.84)

# AC3: 70 days, 0.01 remaining -> 0.01
dl = days_left(date(2027,3,11), date(2027,1,1))
rem = remaining_units(to_units(60), to_units(59.99))
check("S-1 AC3 remaining=1 unit", rem, 1)
pace = calc_pace(rem, dl)
check("S-1 AC3 pace=0.01", pace, 0.01)
check("S-1 AC3 remaining display=0.01", to_credits(rem), 0.01)

# AC4: 364 days, 500 remaining -> 9.62
dl = days_left(date(2027,12,30), date(2027,1,1))
check("S-1 AC4 days_left=364", dl, 364)
pace = calc_pace(to_units(500), dl)
check("S-1 AC4 pace=9.62", pace, 9.62)
check("S-1 AC4 not at-risk", is_at_risk(pace), False)

# AC5: req=500, 70 days, earned=0 -> 50.0, at-risk
dl = days_left(date(2027,3,11), date(2027,1,1))
pace = calc_pace(to_units(500), dl)
check("S-1 AC5 pace=50", pace, 50.0)
check("S-1 AC5 at-risk", is_at_risk(pace), True)
check("S-1 AC5 not urgency", is_urgency(dl), False)

# AC6: earned empty->0, req=60, 70 days -> 6.0
pace = calc_pace(to_units(60), 70)
check("S-1 AC6 pace=6", pace, 6.0)

# AC7 (live update): earned changes from 20 to 30 -> 3.0
pace = calc_pace(to_units(30), 70)
check("S-1 AC7 live update pace=3", pace, 3.0)

# ── S-2 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("\n=== S-2: Urgency (<7 days) ===")

# AC1: 6 days, 10 remaining -> urgency, equiv pace 11.67, not at-risk
dl = days_left(date(2027,12,31), date(2027,12,26))
check("S-2 AC1 days_left=6", dl, 6)
check("S-2 AC1 urgency", is_urgency(dl), True)
equiv_pace = calc_pace(to_units(10), dl)
check("S-2 AC1 equiv_pace not at-risk", is_at_risk(equiv_pace), False)
# verify equiv_pace is 11.67 (ceil(1000*7/6)=ceil(1166.67)=1167 units=11.67)
check("S-2 AC1 equiv_pace=11.67", equiv_pace, 11.67)

# AC2: 2 days, 10 remaining -> urgency, equiv pace 35, not at-risk
dl = days_left(date(2027,12,31), date(2027,12,30))
check("S-2 AC2 days_left=2", dl, 2)
check("S-2 AC2 urgency", is_urgency(dl), True)
equiv_pace = calc_pace(to_units(10), dl)
check("S-2 AC2 equiv_pace=35", equiv_pace, 35.0)
check("S-2 AC2 equiv_pace not at-risk", is_at_risk(equiv_pace), False)

# AC3: 1 day, 10 remaining -> urgency, today, at-risk (equiv pace 70)
dl = days_left(date(2027,12,31), date(2027,12,31))
check("S-2 AC3 days_left=1", dl, 1)
check("S-2 AC3 urgency", is_urgency(dl), True)
equiv_pace = calc_pace(to_units(10), dl)
check("S-2 AC3 equiv_pace=70", equiv_pace, 70.0)
check("S-2 AC3 at-risk", is_at_risk(equiv_pace), True)

# AC4: 7 days, 10 remaining -> NOT urgency, weekly pace 10.0
dl = days_left(date(2027,12,31), date(2027,12,25))
check("S-2 AC4 days_left=7", dl, 7)
check("S-2 AC4 not urgency", is_urgency(dl), False)
pace = calc_pace(to_units(10), dl)
check("S-2 AC4 pace=10", pace, 10.0)

# ── S-3 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("\n=== S-3: Requirement met ===")

# AC1: earned=60, req=60 -> met, extra=0
check("S-3 AC1 met", 60 >= 60, True)
check("S-3 AC1 extra=0", 60 - 60, 0)

# AC2: earned=65, req=60 -> met, extra=5
check("S-3 AC2 met", 65 >= 60, True)
check("S-3 AC2 extra=5", 65 - 60, 5)

# AC3: deadline passed but earned>=required -> requirement met takes priority
# (priority order logic: check met first regardless of dates)
check("S-3 AC3 met before deadline-passed", 60 >= 60, True)

# AC4: earned=59.99 < 60 -> NOT met
check("S-3 AC4 not met", 59.99 >= 60, False)

# ── S-4 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("\n=== S-4: Deadline passed ===")

# AC1: calc-from=Jan 1 2028, end=Dec 31 2027 -> 1 day ago
da = days_ago(date(2027,12,31), date(2028,1,1))
check("S-4 AC1 days_ago=1", da, 1)

# AC2: calc-from=Jan 31 2028, end=Dec 31 2027 -> 31 days ago
da = days_ago(date(2027,12,31), date(2028,1,31))
check("S-4 AC2 days_ago=31", da, 31)

# AC3: earned>=required -> requirement met, not deadline-passed
check("S-4 AC3 met not deadline-passed", 60 >= 60, True)

# ── S-5 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("\n=== S-5: At-risk warning ===")

# AC1: req=500, earned=100, 70 days -> pace=40.0, NOT at-risk
dl = days_left(date(2027,3,11), date(2027,1,1))
pace = calc_pace(to_units(400), dl)
check("S-5 AC1 pace=40", pace, 40.0)
check("S-5 AC1 not at-risk (exactly 40)", is_at_risk(pace), False)

# AC2: req=500, earned=99, 70 days -> pace=40.1, at-risk
pace = calc_pace(to_units(401), dl)
check("S-5 AC2 pace=40.1", pace, 40.1)
check("S-5 AC2 at-risk", is_at_risk(pace), True)

# AC3: 1 day, req=60, earned=50 -> urgency today, equiv pace=70, at-risk
dl = days_left(date(2027,12,31), date(2027,12,31))
equiv_pace = calc_pace(to_units(10), dl)
check("S-5 AC3 equiv_pace=70", equiv_pace, 70.0)
check("S-5 AC3 at-risk", is_at_risk(equiv_pace), True)
check("S-5 AC3 urgency", is_urgency(dl), True)

# AC4: earned=60, req=60 -> met, no at-risk warning
check("S-5 AC4 met no warning", 60 >= 60, True)

# AC5: deadline passed -> no at-risk warning
da = days_ago(date(2027,12,31), date(2028,1,31))
check("S-5 AC5 deadline passed (days_ago=31)", da, 31)

import sys
from datetime import date

# ── core calculation functions ───────────────────────────────────────────────

def days_left(end, frm):
    """Inclusive day count: end_date - calc_from_date + 1."""
    return (end - frm).days + 1

def days_ago(end, frm):
    """calc_from_date - end_date (deadline already passed)."""
    return (frm - end).days

def to_units(credits):
    """Credits -> integer hundredths."""
    return round(credits * 100)

def to_credits(units):
    return units / 100

def remaining_units(req_units, earned_units):
    return max(req_units - earned_units, 0)

def calc_pace(rem_units, dl):
    """Ceiling division in integer hundredths -> display credits (float)."""
    numerator = rem_units * 7
    pace_units = (numerator + dl - 1) // dl
    return to_credits(pace_units)

def is_urgency(dl):
    return dl < 7

def is_at_risk(pace):
    return pace > 40

def fmt(n):
    """Format: trailing zeros dropped, singular for 1."""
    s = f"{n:.2f}".rstrip('0').rstrip('.')
    return s

    global failures

        print(f"       expected {expected!r}, got {got!r}")
    checks.append(ok)

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The session continued from a previous conversation that produced three product documents and a CLAUDE.md for a browser-based recertification pace calculator called "Renewal Runway." No source code has been written yet. In this session the user submitted seven specific fix requests against `docs/user-stories.md` and `CLAUDE.md`:

   1. **S-1 at-risk bug** — S-1 AC6 (500 credits, 70 days → 50/week) said "no error at the upper boundary" but 50 > 40 triggers the at-risk warning. Fix the criterion to show the warning.
   2. **Exact UI text** — "a field-level error appears" is not testable. Write the exact message string for every validation condition and every result state (requirement met, deadline passed, urgency, weekly pace, at-risk warning).
   3. **Credits remaining + days left in panel** — alongside any pace result the panel must always show labeled "X credits remaining" and "X days left" items so users can trust the pace number.
   4. **Drop Feb 30 / add new validation cases** — Feb 30 cannot be typed in a date picker so a reviewer cannot test it. Replace with: empty end date behavior, year out of range (use 1999 and 2101), earned = "abc", 2 decimal max (60.555), calculate-from cleared.
   5. **Pull validation into its own story** — validation ACs come out of S-1; S-1 gets a "change earned → result updates live" criterion instead.
   6. **Reorder stories** — implemented stories first, not-implemented stories after.
   7. **Classic script + tests** — ES modules don't load from `file://`, so `calc.js` must be a classic script with a conditional `module.exports` at the bottom for Node.js. Add `node --test src/calc.test.js` (Node's built-in runner, no npm install). One test per AC with exact numbers. Update CLAUDE.md.

   After making all doc changes: re-verify every number with a script and show the output.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Recertification pace calculation**: `pace = remaining ÷ days_left × 7`, rounded **up** (ceiling) to 2 decimal places
   - **Integer hundredths arithmetic**: credits stored as integer hundredths (1.5 credits = 150 units); ceiling division via `(numerator + days - 1) // days`
   - **Inclusive day counting**: `days_left = end_date − calculate_from_date + 1` (both endpoints counted)
   - **At-risk threshold**: pace strictly > 40 (exactly 40 is NOT at-risk)
   - **Results panel state machine** (priority order): (1) Requirement met, (2) Deadline passed, (3) Urgency < 7 days, (4) Weekly pace. At-risk warning overlays states 3 and 4 only.
   - **Panel secondary items**: in urgency and weekly pace states the panel always shows "X credits remaining" and "X days left" alongside the main result line; these are absent in requirement met and deadline passed states.
   - **Exact UI strings**: both error messages and result state messages are now defined precisely in the Calculation Rules section of user-stories.md, not as vague descriptions.
   - **Classic script compatibility**: `calc.js` uses no `import`/`export`; exports are gated with `if (typeof module !== 'undefined') { module.exports = {...}; }` so it works both as a `<script src>` from `file://` and via `require()` in Node.js tests.
   - **Node.js built-in test runner**: `node --test src/calc.test.js` — no npm, no install.
   - **Leap year counting**: Feb 28 → Mar 1 is 3 days in 2028 (leap) and 2 days in 2027 (non-leap), which affects urgency state (both < 7 days).

# Renewal Runway — Jobs To Be Done

## J-1 · Plan a manageable training pace (R-1 Certified Professional)

When I am part-way through my recertification cycle and unsure how much training I still need to do, I want to know how many credits I need to earn per week from now until my deadline, so I can fit learning around work at a steady rate instead of rushing at the end.

## J-2 · Quickly assess whether a late renewal is still realistic (R-1 Certified Professional)

When my deadline is close and I know I am behind on credits, I want to know immediately whether hitting the required total in the time remaining is feasible, so I can decide whether to clear my calendar, pursue an exam route, or plan around the grace period.

## J-3 · Confirm the requirement is met and close the loop (R-1 Certified Professional)

When I have earned most of my credits and believe I may have reached the required total, I want to confirm my earned credits meet or exceed the requirement, so I can stop tracking and submit my renewal with confidence.

## J-4 · Spot at-risk team members before it is too late (R-2 L&D Manager)

When I am reviewing my team's professional development status, I want to know which team members are unlikely to reach their recertification requirement by their deadline, so I can act while there is still enough time for training to make a difference.

## J-5 · Plan training allocation for a future quarter (R-2 L&D Manager)

When I am deciding how to allocate training time and budget for an upcoming quarter, I want to know what pace a team member would need to meet their recertification requirement if their dedicated learning time started then rather than now, so I can compare options and commit resources to where they will have the most impact.

# Renewal Runway — App Roles

## R-1 · Certified Professional

A Certified Professional is a credentialed HR or project-management practitioner who is responsible for renewing their own certification before their cycle ends. They know their total credit requirement and their cycle end date, and they check in on their own progress when they feel uncertain about whether they are keeping up. They can enter their certification details — credits required, credits already earned, and cycle end date — and see their required weekly pace from today and a risk assessment for their renewal. They must never be told they are on track, or that their renewal is complete, when their actual credit figures say otherwise.

## R-2 · L&D Manager

An L&D Manager is a learning-and-development or team manager who monitors recertification progress for people who report to them. They are checking someone else's renewal: they read credit figures from that person's certification portal and work in quarterly planning windows rather than reacting to today's status. They can enter a team member's certification details and choose a future "calculate from" date to model what pace the team member would need if training time started next quarter or later. Their primary output is the risk flag — they use it to decide where to direct training budget and protected learning time. They must never receive a result that shows a renewal as low-risk or on track when the underlying figures indicate the team member is at risk of missing their deadline.

For failed deployments, inspect state and build logs. For production errors, start with get_runtime_errors, then get_runtime_logs.

Use supported project/deployment/environment/time filters. Follow pagination for complete results; report partial data. Inspect every result. Distinguish observed failures from suspected causes.

4	
5	These rules govern every result the app produces. All stories are written against them.
6	
7	**Credit precision**

9	
10	**Credits remaining**  
11	`remaining = max(required − earned, 0)`. When earned ≥ required the result is 0 for pace purposes; the panel shows the requirement-met state instead.
12	
13	**Days left**  
14	`days_left = end_date − calculate_from_date + 1` (both dates inclusive).  
15	Example: Dec 29 → Dec 31 = 3 days. This reflects that credits can be earned on the last day of the cycle.
16	
17	**Weekly pace**  
18	`pace = remaining ÷ days_left × 7`, rounded **up** to 2 decimal places. Rounding up ensures that sustaining the shown pace always finishes on time.
19	
20	**Date display**  
21	Calendar dates only; no time-of-day or time-zone handling. Shown as "Dec 31, 2027".
22	
23	**Number display**  
24	Up to 2 decimal places; trailing zeros dropped (4.00 → 4, 3.90 → 3.9); thousands separators applied. Exactly 1 uses the singular form ("1 credit", "1 day"); all other quantities use the plural.
25

27	Results update as fields change. There is no separate calculate button.
28

31

34	
35	| Preset | Credits required |
36	|---|---|
37	| SHRM-CP / SHRM-SCP | 60 |
38	| HRCI PHR / SPHR | 60 |
39	| PMI PMP | 60 |
40	| PMI CAPM | 15 |
41	| Custom | (user-entered) |
42	
43	Presets cover totals only; category or activity-type breakdowns are out of scope.
44

52	| Calculate-from date | Valid calendar date, year 2000–2100 |
53	
54	**Default state (on load and after reset)**

|---|---|
| Requirement met (earned > required) | "Requirement met. You have {earned} of {required} credits ({extra} extra)." |
| Requirement met (earned = required) | "Requirement met. You have {earned} of {required} credits." |
| Deadline passed | "Cycle ended on {date} ({N} day[s] ago)." |
| Urgency, days > 1 | "You need {remaining} credits in the next {N} days." |
| Urgency, days = 1 | "You need {remaining} credits today." |
| Weekly pace | "{pace} credits per week" |
| At-risk warning (above state 3 or 4) | "At risk: this pace exceeds 40 credits per week." |

---

## Results panel — priority order

When credits required and cycle end date are both valid, the panel shows exactly one of these states, checked in this order:

1. **Requirement met** — earned ≥ required. Shown even if the deadline has passed.
2. **Deadline passed** — cycle end date is before the calculate-from date and requirement not met.
3. **Urgency** — days left < 7 and requirement not met.
4. **Weekly pace** — all other cases.

An at-risk warning appears above the result for states 3 and 4 when the weekly pace exceeds 40. A pace of exactly 40 is not at risk.

---

Each story below names the job it serves. Status reflects what the app does today. Implemented stories are listed first.

# Renewal Runway — Recertification Pace Calculator

A browser-based tool for professionals tracking continuing education credits toward credential renewal. Enter how many credits you need, how many you have, and your cycle end date — it tells you the weekly pace required to finish on time.

**Why this over a generic calculator?** KnowledgeCity's learners renew SHRM, HRCI, and PMI credentials on three-year cycles. Most start tracking late and need a quick answer to "am I on pace?" — not a spreadsheet. Renewal Runway handles the edge cases (less than a week left, requirement already met, deadline passed) and flags an at-risk pace before it becomes a crisis.

---

## Prerequisites

| Purpose | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Running the app | Any current Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari |
| Running the tests | Node.js 18 or later |

No install, no build step, no internet connection required.

---

## Running the app

Double-click `src/index.html` or open it in a browser:

```
src/index.html
```

---

## Running the tests

```
node --test src/calc.test.js
```

52 tests covering the calculation and validation logic in `src/calc.js` for user stories S-1 through S-7 (input validation, pace calculation, result states, edge cases). **S-8 (certification presets) and S-9 (reset button)** involve DOM interactions and were verified by hand in the browser — they are not in the automated suite.

---

## Project docs

- [App roles](docs/app-roles.md)
- [Jobs to be done](docs/jobs-to-be-done.md)
- [User stories and acceptance criteria](docs/user-stories.md)

## Session transcript

- [Session 01](transcripts/session-01.md)

---

## AI tool and model

Built with **Claude Code** using **Claude Opus 5.5**.

## Code changed by hand

None. All code was generated by Claude Code and committed as-is after test verification and browser testing.

---

## Assumptions

- **Totals only** — the calculator tracks overall credit totals. Category sub-requirements (e.g. SHRM's PDC mix or PMI's Talent Triangle splits) are out of scope.
- **1 credit ≈ 1 contact hour** — the at-risk threshold of 40 credits/week is treated as equivalent to full-time study. Pace above that is flagged as at-risk.
- **Both dates are inclusive** — a cycle running Dec 29 to Dec 31 has 3 days remaining, not 2.
- **Pace rounds up** — the displayed weekly pace always guarantees completion by the deadline; it never rounds down.
- **"Calculate from" defaults to today** — re-read at page load and again when Reset is pressed, so the default is always the current date.
- **Preset credit totals** — SHRM-CP/SCP 60, HRCI PHR/SPHR 60, PMI PMP 60, PMI CAPM 15. These reflect published renewal requirements as of November 2026.

# Renewal Runway — Recertification Pace Calculator

A browser-based tool for professionals tracking continuing education credits toward credential renewal. Enter how many credits you need, how many you have, and your cycle end date — it tells you the weekly pace required to finish on time.

**Why this over a generic calculator?** KnowledgeCity's learners renew SHRM, HRCI, and PMI credentials on three-year cycles. Many leave it to the last few months and need a quick answer to "am I on pace?" — not a spreadsheet. Renewal Runway handles the edge cases (less than a week left, requirement already met, deadline passed) and flags an at-risk pace before it becomes a crisis.

---

## Prerequisites

| Purpose | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Running the app | Any current Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari |
| Running the tests | Node.js 18 or later |

No install, no build step, no internet connection required.

---

## Running the app

Double-click `src/index.html` or open it in a browser:

```
src/index.html
```

---

## Running the tests

```
node --test src/calc.test.js
```

52 tests covering the calculation and validation logic in `src/calc.js` for user stories S-1 through S-7 (input validation, pace calculation, result states, edge cases). **S-8 (certification presets) and S-9 (reset button)** involve DOM interactions and were verified by hand in the browser — they are not in the automated suite.

1	# Renewal Runway — User Stories
2	
3	## Calculation Rules
4	
5	These rules govern every result the app produces. All stories are written against them.
6	
7	**Credit precision**  
8	Credits are stored as integer hundredths (1.5 credits = 150 units). All arithmetic uses integers, eliminating floating-point errors.
9	
10	**Credits remaining**  
11	`remaining = max(required − earned, 0)`. When earned ≥ required the result is 0 for pace purposes; the panel shows the requirement-met state instead.
12	
13	**Days left**  
14	`days_left = end_date − calculate_from_date + 1` (both dates inclusive).  
15	Example: Dec 29 → Dec 31 = 3 days. This reflects that credits can be earned on the last day of the cycle.
16	
17	**Weekly pace**  
18	`pace = remaining ÷ days_left × 7`, rounded **up** to 2 decimal places. Rounding up ensures that sustaining the shown pace always finishes on time.
19	
20	**Date display**  
21	Calendar dates only; no time-of-day or time-zone handling. Shown as "Dec 31, 2027".
22	
23	**Number display**  
24	Up to 2 decimal places; trailing zeros dropped (4.00 → 4, 3.90 → 3.9); thousands separators applied. Exactly 1 uses the singular form ("1 credit", "1 day"); all other quantities use the plural.
25	
26	**Live updates**  
27	Results update as fields change. There is no separate calculate button.
28	
29	**Panel display**  
30	In the Urgency and Weekly pace states, the panel shows three items below any at-risk warning: the main result line, then "X credits remaining" (or "1 credit remaining"), then "X days left" (or "1 day left"). These secondary items are not shown in the Requirement met or Deadline passed states.
31	
32	**Certification presets**  
33	Selecting a preset fills credits required. Manually editing credits required switches the selector to Custom.
34	
35	| Preset | Credits required |
36	|---|---|
37	| SHRM-CP / SHRM-SCP | 60 |
38	| HRCI PHR / SPHR | 60 |
39	| PMI PMP | 60 |
40	| PMI CAPM | 15 |
41	| Custom | (user-entered) |
42	
43	Presets cover totals only; category or activity-type breakdowns are out of scope.
44	
45	**Field limits**
46	
47	| Field | Valid range |
48	|---|---|
49	| Credits required | > 0 and ≤ 500, up to 2 decimal places |
50	| Credits earned | ≥ 0 and ≤ 1,000, up to 2 decimal places |
51	| Cycle end date | Valid calendar date, year 2000–2100 |
52	| Calculate-from date | Valid calendar date, year 2000–2100 |
53	
54	**Default state (on load and after reset)**  
55	Preset: Custom. Credits required: empty. Credits earned: 0. Cycle end date: empty. Calculate-from date: current date. No result is shown until credits required and cycle end date are both filled with valid values.
56	
57	**UI text — error messages**
58	
59	| Condition | Message |
60	|---|---|
61	| Credits required empty | (no error; result not shown until a valid value is entered) |
62	| Credits required = 0 or negative | "Credits required must be greater than 0." |
63	| Credits required > 500 | "Credits required cannot exceed 500." |
64	| Credits required non-numeric | "Credits required must be a number." |
65	| Credits required more than 2 decimal places | "Credits required cannot have more than 2 decimal places." |
66	| Credits earned negative | "Credits earned cannot be negative." |
67	| Credits earned > 1,000 | "Credits earned cannot exceed 1,000." |
68	| Credits earned non-numeric | "Credits earned must be a number." |
69	| Credits earned more than 2 decimal places | "Credits earned cannot have more than 2 decimal places." |
70	| Cycle end date empty | (no error; result not shown until a valid value is entered) |
71	| Cycle end date is a calendar-impossible date (e.g. Feb 30) | "Cycle end date is not a valid calendar date." |
72	| Cycle end date year < 2000 or > 2100 | "Cycle end date must be between 2000 and 2100." |
73	| Calculate-from date cleared | "Calculate-from date is required." |
74	
75	**UI text — result states**
76	
77	| State | Panel content |
78	|---|---|
79	| Empty (credits required or end date not yet filled) | "Enter credits required and your cycle end date to see your pace." |
80	| Error (one or more fields are invalid) | "Fix the highlighted field to see your pace." |
81	| Requirement met (earned > required) | "Requirement met. You have {earned} of {required} credits ({extra} extra)." |
82	| Requirement met (earned = required) | "Requirement met. You have {earned} of {required} credits." |
83	| Deadline passed | "Cycle ended on {date} ({N} day[s] ago)." |
84	| Urgency, days > 1 | "You need {remaining} credits in the next {N} days." |
85	| Urgency, days = 1 | "You need {remaining} credits today." |
86	| Weekly pace | "{pace} credits per week" |
87	| At-risk warning (above state 3 or 4) | "At risk: this pace exceeds 40 credits per week." |
88	
89	---
90	
91	## Results panel — priority order
92	
93	When credits required and cycle end date are both valid, the panel shows exactly one of these states, checked in this order:
94	
95	1. **Requirement met** — earned ≥ required. Shown even if the deadline has passed.
96	2. **Deadline passed** — cycle end date is before the calculate-from date and requirement not met.
97	3. **Urgency** — days left < 7 and requirement not met.
98	4. **Weekly pace** — all other cases.
99	
100	An at-risk warning appears above the result for states 3 and 4 when the weekly pace exceeds 40. A pace of exactly 40 is not at risk.
101	
102	---
103	
104	Each story below names the job it serves. Status reflects what the app does today. Implemented stories are listed first.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## S-1 · Enter certification details and see weekly pace
109	**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Implemented
110	
111	As a Certified Professional, I want to enter my total credits required, credits already earned, and certification cycle end date and see the weekly pace I need from today, so that I can plan how many hours of training to schedule each week.
112	
113	**Acceptance criteria**
114	
115	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027 (70 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 20, then the panel shows **"4 credits per week"**, **"40 credits remaining"**, **"70 days left"** (remaining 40 ÷ 70 × 7 = 4.0, trailing zero dropped).
116	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 14, 2027 (73 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 20, then the panel shows **"3.84 credits per week"**, **"40 credits remaining"**, **"73 days left"** (40 ÷ 73 × 7 = 3.836…, rounded up to 3.84).
117	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027 (70 days); required = 60; earned = 59.99, then the panel shows **"0.01 credits per week"**, **"0.01 credits remaining"**, **"70 days left"** (remaining 0.01 ÷ 70 × 7 = 0.001…, rounded up to 0.01).
118	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Dec 30, 2027 (364 days); required = 500; earned = 0, then the panel shows **"9.62 credits per week"**, **"500 credits remaining"**, **"364 days left"** (500 ÷ 364 × 7 = 9.615…, rounded up), confirming the app handles maximum field values without error.
119	- Given credits required = 500; calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027 (70 days); earned = 0, then the at-risk warning appears and the panel shows **"50 credits per week"**, **"500 credits remaining"**, **"70 days left"** (500 ÷ 70 × 7 = 50.0; 50 > 40).
120	- Given credits earned is left empty; calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027; required = 60, then earned is treated as 0 and the panel shows **"6 credits per week"**, **"60 credits remaining"**, **"70 days left"** (60 ÷ 70 × 7 = 6.0).
121	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027; required = 60; earned = 20 (result showing), when earned changes to 30, then the result updates immediately to **"3 credits per week"**, **"30 credits remaining"**, **"70 days left"** (remaining 30 ÷ 70 × 7 = 3.0).
122	- Given credits required is empty (and no other errors are present), then the panel shows **"Enter credits required and your cycle end date to see your pace."** — no error, no result.
123	
124	---
125	
126	## S-2 · See an urgency message when fewer than 7 days remain
127	**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-2 | **Status:** Implemented
128	
129	As a Certified Professional, I want to see the credits I still need stated in days rather than weeks when my deadline is very close, so that I can judge immediately whether catching up is still feasible.
130	
131	**Acceptance criteria**
132	
133	- Given calc-from = Dec 26, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027 (6 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 50, then the panel shows **"You need 10 credits in the next 6 days."**, **"10 credits remaining"**, **"6 days left"**, with no at-risk warning (equivalent pace 10 ÷ 6 × 7 = 11.67, which is ≤ 40).
134	- Given calc-from = Dec 30, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027 (2 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 50, then the panel shows **"You need 10 credits in the next 2 days."**, **"10 credits remaining"**, **"2 days left"**, with no at-risk warning (equivalent pace 10 ÷ 2 × 7 = 35, which is ≤ 40).
135	- Given calc-from = Dec 31, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027 (1 day inclusive); required = 60; earned = 50, then the at-risk warning appears and the panel shows **"You need 10 credits today."**, **"10 credits remaining"**, **"1 day left"** (equivalent pace 10 ÷ 1 × 7 = 70, which is > 40).
136	- Given calc-from = Dec 25, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027 (7 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 50, then the panel shows the weekly pace **"10 credits per week"**, **"10 credits remaining"**, **"7 days left"** (10 ÷ 7 × 7 = 10.0) — urgency is not triggered at exactly 7 days.
137	
138	---
139	
140	## S-3 · Confirm that the credit requirement is met
141	**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-3 | **Status:** Implemented
142	
143	As a Certified Professional, I want to see a clear confirmation when my earned credits meet or exceed the total required, so that I can submit my renewal without second-guessing the numbers.
144	
145	**Acceptance criteria**
146	
147	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 60, then the panel shows **"Requirement met. You have 60 of 60 credits."**
148	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 65, then the panel shows **"Requirement met. You have 65 of 60 credits (5 extra)."**
149	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2028; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 60 (deadline already passed), then the panel shows the requirement-met message — not the deadline-passed message.
150	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027 (70 days); required = 60; earned = 59.99, then the requirement-met message is **not** shown and the panel shows **"0.01 credits per week"** instead (59.99 < 60).
151	
152	---
153	
154	## S-4 · Know when the cycle has ended without the requirement being met
155	**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-2 | **Status:** Implemented
156	
157	As a Certified Professional, I want to know clearly when my certification cycle has ended without my having met the credit requirement, so that I understand my situation and can decide what to do next.
158	
159	**Acceptance criteria**
160	
161	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2028; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 50, then the panel shows **"Cycle ended on Dec 31, 2027 (1 day ago)."** with no pace shown (Jan 1, 2028 − Dec 31, 2027 = 1 day).
162	- Given calc-from = Jan 31, 2028; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 50, then the panel shows **"Cycle ended on Dec 31, 2027 (31 days ago)."**
163	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2028; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 60, then the requirement-met message is shown — not the deadline-passed message.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## S-5 · See an at-risk warning when the required pace is unsustainable
168	**Role:** L&D Manager | **Job:** J-4 | **Status:** Implemented
169	
170	As an L&D Manager, I want to see a prominent at-risk warning when the credits-per-week pace exceeds 40, so that I can immediately identify a team member who needs intervention before it is too late.
171	
172	**Acceptance criteria**
173	
174	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027 (70 days); required = 500; earned = 100, then the panel shows **"40 credits per week"**, **"400 credits remaining"**, **"70 days left"** with **no at-risk warning** (remaining 400 ÷ 70 × 7 = 40.0; exactly 40 is not at risk).
175	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027 (70 days); required = 500; earned = 99, then the **at-risk warning "At risk: this pace exceeds 40 credits per week."** appears above **"40.1 credits per week"**, **"401 credits remaining"**, **"70 days left"** (remaining 401 ÷ 70 × 7 = 40.1).
176	- Given calc-from = Dec 31, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027 (1 day); required = 60; earned = 50, then the **at-risk warning** appears above **"You need 10 credits today."**, **"10 credits remaining"**, **"1 day left"** (equivalent pace 10 ÷ 1 × 7 = 70).
177	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 60, then no at-risk warning appears (requirement already met).
178	- Given calc-from = Jan 31, 2028; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 50, then no at-risk warning appears (deadline-passed state).
179	
180	---
181	
182	## S-6 · Set a future calculate-from date to model a later start
183	**Role:** L&D Manager | **Job:** J-5 | **Status:** Implemented
184	
185	As an L&D Manager, I want to set the calculate-from date to a future date, so that I can model the pace a team member would need if their dedicated training time started next quarter and decide where to commit budget before the quarter begins.
186	
187	**Acceptance criteria**
188	
189	- Given calc-from = Dec 1, 2027; end = Jan 9, 2028 (40 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 20, then the panel shows **"7 credits per week"**, **"40 credits remaining"**, **"40 days left"** (40 ÷ 40 × 7 = 7.0) — this is the reference result showing calculate-from affects days_left.
190	- Given calc-from = Apr 1, 2027; end = Jun 29, 2027 (90 days inclusive); required = 60; earned = 24, then the panel shows **"2.8 credits per week"**, **"36 credits remaining"**, **"90 days left"** (remaining 36 ÷ 90 × 7 = 2.8). With calc-from = Jan 1, 2027 instead (180 days inclusive), the same end date and credits yield **"1.4 credits per week"**, **"36 credits remaining"**, **"180 days left"** (36 ÷ 180 × 7 = 1.4), showing how a later start doubles the required pace.
191	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2028; end = Dec 31, 2027; required = 60; earned = 50, then the deadline-passed state is shown — a calculate-from date after the cycle end is valid input, not an error.
192	- Given calc-from = Feb 28, 2028; end = Mar 1, 2028; required = 60; earned = 57, then the panel shows **"You need 3 credits in the next 3 days."**, **"3 credits remaining"**, **"3 days left"** (Feb 28, Feb 29, Mar 1 = 3 days inclusive — 2028 is a leap year). With calc-from = Feb 28, 2027 and end = Mar 1, 2027 instead, the panel shows **"You need 3 credits in the next 2 days."**, **"3 credits remaining"**, **"2 days left"** (Feb 28, Mar 1 = 2 days — 2027 has no Feb 29), confirming that Feb 29 is counted when it exists.
193	
194	---
195	
196	## S-7 · Input validation
197	**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Implemented
198	
199	As a Certified Professional, I want the app to flag invalid entries immediately with a clear message, so that I am never shown a result based on nonsense inputs and I know exactly what to fix.
200	
201	**Acceptance criteria**
202	
203	- Given credits required = 0, then the error **"Credits required must be greater than 0."** appears and no result is shown.
204	- Given credits required = 501, then the error **"Credits required cannot exceed 500."** appears and no result is shown.
205	- Given credits required = "abc" (non-numeric), then the error **"Credits required must be a number."** appears and no result is shown.
206	- Given credits required = 60.555, then the error **"Credits required cannot have more than 2 decimal places."** appears and no result is shown.
207	- Given credits earned = −1, then the error **"Credits earned cannot be negative."** appears and no result is shown.
208	- Given credits earned = 1,001, then the error **"Credits earned cannot exceed 1,000."** appears and no result is shown.
209	- Given credits earned = "abc" (non-numeric), then the error **"Credits earned must be a number."** appears and no result is shown.
210	- Given credits earned = 60.555, then the error **"Credits earned cannot have more than 2 decimal places."** appears and no result is shown.
211	- Given cycle end date year = 1999, then the error **"Cycle end date must be between 2000 and 2100."** appears and no result is shown.
212	- Given cycle end date year = 2101, then the error **"Cycle end date must be between 2000 and 2100."** appears and no result is shown.
213	- Given the calculate-from date is cleared, then the error **"Calculate-from date is required."** appears and no result is shown.
214	- Given cycle end date is empty and credits required = 60 and calc-from = Jan 1, 2027, then no error appears for the end date field and no result is shown.
215	- Given credits required = 501 (error showing), when credits required is corrected to 60 and end = Mar 11, 2027 and calc-from = Jan 1, 2027 and earned = 20, then the error clears and **"4 credits per week"** appears.
216	- Given calc-from = Jan 1, 2027; end = Mar 11, 2027; required = 60; earned = 20 (result "4 credits per week" is showing), when cycle end date is cleared, then the result disappears immediately and no error is shown for the end date field.
217	
218	---
219	
220	## S-8 · Select a certification preset to fill credits required
221	**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Implemented
222	
223	As a Certified Professional, I want to pick my credential from a list and have the total credits required filled in automatically, so that I do not have to look up the number for my specific certification.
224	
225	**Acceptance criteria**
226	
227	- Given I select SHRM-CP / SHRM-SCP, then credits required is set to 60.
228	- Given I select PMI CAPM, then credits required is set to 15.
229	- Given I select a preset and then manually edit credits required, then the selector switches to Custom.
230	- Given I select a preset, manually edit credits required, and then select the same preset again, then credits required returns to the preset value.
231	
232	---
233	
234	## S-9 · Reset all fields to the default state
235	**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Implemented
236	
237	As a Certified Professional, I want to clear all inputs and return to the starting state, so that I can run a fresh calculation without reloading the page.
238	
239	**Acceptance criteria**
240	
241	- Given any fields have been changed, when I activate reset, then credits required is cleared, credits earned returns to 0, cycle end date is cleared, calculate-from date returns to the current date (read at reset time, not page-load time), and the preset selector returns to Custom.
242	- Given a result or error is currently shown, when I activate reset, then it is cleared immediately and no result is shown.

247	**Role:** L&D Manager | **Job:** J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented
248	
249	As an L&D Manager, I want to enter details for several team members in one view and see them ranked by risk, so that I can prioritise training budget across the team without running separate calculations.

254	- Given a team member's data changes, then their position in the ranked list updates immediately.

260	
261	As a Certified Professional, I want to enter my credits broken down by required category so that I can confirm I have met each category minimum, not just the overall total.

265	- Given a PMP credential with Ways of Working, Power Skills, and Business Acumen minimums, when I enter credits by category, then I see whether each minimum is satisfied alongside the overall total.
266	- Given an HRCI credential with an ethics credit requirement, when I enter my credits, then the ethics component is verified separately from the total.

271	**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented
272	
273	As a Certified Professional, I want my certification details to be remembered when I return to the app, so that I do not have to re-enter them every time I check my pace.

276	
277	- Given I have entered credits required, credits earned, and a cycle end date, when I close and reopen the app, then those values are restored and the result is shown immediately.
278	- Given I activate reset, when I close and reopen the app, then no saved values are restored and the app shows the default state.
279	
280	---
281	
282	## S-13 · See how many courses to complete each week
283	**Role:** Certified Professional | **Job:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented
284	
285	As a Certified Professional, I want to see my weekly pace expressed as a number of courses, not just credits, so that I can turn the target into a concrete item on my calendar.

288	
289	- Given a weekly pace of 2 credits and a typical course length of 1 credit, then the result shows "2 courses per week" alongside the credit pace.
